summary.text: A 55-year-old Asian woman presented with left facial pain and an unremarkable medical history. About 3 years earlier she had nonsurgical root canal treatment of the maxillary first and second molars (#26 and #27). Examination found normal probing depths, no buccal gingival swelling and no percussion sensitivity; radiograph and CBCT showed periradicular radiolucency, a periradicular lesion, mucosal edema in the left maxillary sinus and an almost indiscernible maxillary sinus floor.

MSEO with a periapical abscess originating from tooth #26 was diagnosed, a surgical approach was ruled out because of the risk of endo-antral communication, and nonsurgical root canal treatment was planned. Tooth #26 was treated under 2% lidocaine with epinephrine by removing the filling, irrigating with 5% sodium hypochlorite and placing calcium hydroxide medicament; at the next visit symptoms had decreased and the canals were filled and restored, and tooth #27 was treated.

Two months later symptoms had resolved and zirconia crowns were placed on teeth #26 and #27. At 6 months she reported facial fullness; radiograph showed no bony healing while CBCT showed reestablishment of the cortical maxillary sinus floor with unchanged edema and lesion size. Surgery was planned and performed with flap reflection, enucleation, buccal root-end resection, ultrasonic root-end preparation and MTA filling; the excised tissue was a radicular cyst with chronic inflammation and cholesterol crystals.

Two years after surgery she had no symptoms, and radiograph and CBCT showed bony healing around the roots of tooth #26, resolved mucosal edema, a well-reestablished maxillary sinus floor and no radiographic pathosis on periapical radiography. A well-demarcated radiolucency remained around the buccal aspect of the palatal root, where root-end surgery was not performed, and ongoing follow-up was considered necessary.
